title: Signal Curator — Spark Scan: Consolidation pipeline and initial acceptance criteria for Sales/CS enterprise requests
creator: Marina Lopez
description: Problem: Sales and CS submit high-volume feature signals that arrive as long freeform emails, Slack threads, or spreadsheets. Current intake routes duplicate asks, creates noisy triage work, and blocks fast economic/feasibility decisions for large accounts. Goal: build a lightweight consolidation pipeline ("Spark Scan") for Sales/CS to surface bundled enterprise asks, produce a quick economic feasibility snapshot, and emit a standardized ticket with acceptance criteria for PM/Eng evaluation. This ticket defines the pipeline, scoring heuristic, minimum enrichment steps, and initial engineering signals required to move a bundle into a scoped PRD candidate.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable pipeline that accepts batched Sales/CS signals (CSV/Drive link/Slack thread) and returns a consolidated bundle summary in under 48 hours.

Each bundle output includes: top-3 proposed solution themes, estimated 1-year incremental revenue / cost proxy, rough engineering complexity flag (Low/Medium/High), and recommended next owner (PM/SE/Eng).
A scoring card is attached to every output with visible weights and the raw inputs used to calculate score.
Bundle outputs create a standardized Linear draft ticket pre-populated with title, description, labels, suggested estimate and dependencies.
Pilot run with three Sales/CS teams (North America, EMEA, Strategic accounts) completed and a post-pilot synthesis documented.
triage_flow: Intake: Sales rep uploads signal bundle using a standard form or Drive folder and tags #spark-scan.
Normalization: PM-run enrichment step to canonicalize account, product area, and ask category (automated heuristics + manual verification).
Deduplication: fuzzy-match against existing tickets and recent bundles (30d window).
Scoring: run quick-econ and effort heuristic to assign initial priority and customer_impact label.
Output: create draft Linear ticket + notification to assigned PM for decision within 3 business days.
scoring_rubric: Customer ARR signal (weight 30%): account tier * expressed dollar ask (banded)
Urgency / Time-to-value (weight 20%): customer deadline or deployment constraint
Strategic fit (weight 20%): aligns to active roadmap themes in 'Enterprise Platform'
Implementation complexity (weight -15%): engineering complexity penalty (Low=0, Med=-10, High=-30)
Unique technical blocker (weight -15%): regulatory/compliance requirement that raises cost
initial_feasibility_signals: Model serving change required? (yes/no) — quick note from infra/serving on compatibility
Data residency or KMS requirement — flag for Private deployment review
Potential model/quantization changes: trivial / moderate / significant
Ops impact: new telemetry, new dashboards, or rollout policy changes?
decisions: We will treat Spark Scan as a PM-owned lightweight curator (not an engineering backlog automator). PMs decide canonicalization rules and aggregation thresholds.
For pilot, only surface bundles with combined score >= 40 (out of 100) to reduce noise for Eng review.
Bundle outputs must include a minimum of one customer quote and a linked ticket stub from the originating Sales rep.
notes: Avoid building heavy ML deduplication for MVP; start with rule-based heuristics + simple fuzzy match and iterate if false positive rate > 20%.
Keep the economic estimator conservative — use banded ranges and explicit assumptions in each output to avoid overstating ROI.
Pilot scope limited to feature-ask bundles (not bugs, not legal/compliance requests). Separate path for SOC2/regulatory asks.
